input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
input.rationale: The only liability ceiling in the Agreement (p0077, in the indemnity section) protects TrueLink alone and is further narrowed to matters "ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11", sections that do not exist in this document. Client's liability — including the broad indemnity in Section 12a and its confidentiality obligations — is entirely unlimited, and there is no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere (searches for "consequential", "indirect" and "liability" return only p0041, p0042 and p0077). A one-way cap with the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory, so this fails the fallback on a material term. We target the fallback: the existing 12-month compensation basis is retained, the cap is made mutual and aggregate for the whole Agreement, and indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct sit outside it. We have not pressed the preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, the mutual consequential-damages waiver or the data-protection/fraud/IP and payment-obligation carve-outs; those remain available if TrueLink prefers a fuller clause.

proposal.summary: Make the liability cap mutual and aggregate across the Agreement, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made the cap mutual and aggregate for the whole Agreement (the current cap protects only TrueLink and cross-refers to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11, which do not exist), and we placed indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside it. This is our fallback position: Client's liability cannot be unlimited while TrueLink's is capped at 12 months' compensation.
